title: How Much Memory Does Your AI Agent Actually Need?
summary: The article explores how the optimal amount of 'agentic memory' (self-distilled guidelines from past tasks) varies depending on the AI model's capability. It introduces ALTK-Evolve, a framework that enables agents to learn from their own trajectories without weight updates or human annotation. The research identifies three patterns: strong models benefit from full guideline sets, weaker models perform best with curated retrieval (a compact core plus task-relevant guidelines), and saturated models show no measurable gain. The study also highlights that curated retrieval can improve performance while minimizing token costs, especially when combined with prompt caching.
key_points: Agentic memory is not a one-size-fits-all feature; its effectiveness depends on the model's capability and headroom.

Three observed patterns: (1) Strong models with headroom benefit from the full guideline set, (2) Weaker models perform best with curated retrieval (compact core + task-relevant guidelines), (3) Saturated models show no measurable improvement.
Curated retrieval can be both the most accurate and cost-effective option, e.g., gpt-oss-120b gained +16.1pp in task completion with only a +5% increase in tokens.
Prompt caching significantly reduces the cost of injecting full guideline sets in production environments.
The study evaluated 8 models on AppWorld, a benchmark with 585 multi-step tasks, using metrics like Task Goal Completion (TGC) and Scenario Goal Completion (SGC).
Memory calibration is critical: weaker models may be overwhelmed by large guideline sets, while strong models can leverage them effectively.
Future work includes developing a learned selector for better guideline retrieval, exploring memory for very weak models, and validating results on broader benchmarks.
